desc: Analyze the problem and identify that it is a Maximum Weight K-Matching problem with a specific weight function.
Determine that for small N, brute-force or exact matching is feasible, while for large N, a heuristic (Binary Search + Greedy) is necessary due to complexity constraints.
Implement the brute-force solver for small N (N <= 20). This will try all possible sets of K disjoint pairs.
Implement the binary search on the answer for larger N. The check function will use dynamic programming on a subset of top cakes.

Re-evaluate the "large N" strategy. Since $N$ can be $10^5$, we cannot generate all pairs. However, note that the optimal pairs likely involve the "top" cakes. We can restrict the candidate set to the top $M$ cakes (e.g., $M=20$) based on the sum of their coordinates. Then run the DP check on this reduced set.
Combine the small N brute-force and the large N heuristic into a single solution.
